item.title: Research Ideas — 2026-09-14
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Wags Postdoc — Research Ideas, 2026-09-14 (Show Notes) 10 ideas. Top pick: a systematic review of the arthroscopic tests used to diagnose foveal TFCC tears — 9 primary reports, and the systematic-review search returns 5 hits, every one of them in the knee, ankle or elbow. The slate is deliberately smaller than last week's 15 so the episode returns to its 15–20 minute target. Every gap below was proven with a live PubMed query and hit count, recorded in full in the report. Ideas are starting points, not protocols; the honesty flags stated in the episode are repeated here. --- Clinical — Shoulder Arthroplasty 1. Does the preoperative plan predict the painful anterior shoulder after reverse arthroplasty? Anterior/coracoid pain now has a denominator — 1.0% prevalence, onset a mean 10 months out, and 49% resolving completely without surgery — with predictors that are almost all surgeon-chosen (subcoracoid distance, anterior glenosphere overhang, calcar distalization). A separate planning-CT model (9 vs 9) reached 79.0% cross-validated accuracy. 38-hit check: neither predictor set has ever been validated, and nobody has tested the plan against the pain. ⚠️ At 1% prevalence this is a validation, not a derivation — possibly two centres. 2 / 2 / 3 Clinical — Rotator Cuff / Tendon Transfer ⭐ 2. What happens to the bone under the transfer? A propensity-matched series (26 pairs from 2,242) found latissimus transfer added to a reverse gave no extra external rotation and no better ASES — but 96% early proximal humeral erosion versus 4%. A 2021 series found osteolysis at the L'Episcopo insertion in 10 of 13 shoulders, 54% severe. The lower trapezius transfer — the one this group performs and publishes — has never had its insertion site examined, and none of the 24 systematic reviews of transfers with reverse arthroplasty reports insertion-site bone. ⚠️ Indication-confounded and non-randomised; pre-specify an erosion grading scale with two blinded readers. 3 / 3 / 3 Clinical — Shoulder Arthroscopy / Neurogenic TOS 3. Does hypermobility change the result of arthroscopic pectoralis minor release? Hypermobility entered the TOS literature through vascular surgery: 28 hEDS patients out of ~1,400 encounters, 78.6% women, a mean of 4.6 prior upper-extremity operations each, and 81.3% improved after decompression — but with no non-hypermobile comparison group, no prospective Beighton scoring, and the arthroscopic operation absent. 8-hit check: no study anywhere reports hypermobility as an outcome predictor after any pectoralis minor release. ⚠️ Must be prospective; covary for prior surgery and comorbidity. 2 / 2 / 3 Clinical — Wrist Arthroscopy 4. The first clinical series of suture-based DRUJ stabilization. The group's own cadaveric study showed a suture-tape/button reconstruction preserves rotation (174° → 175°) and restores translation to intact in neutral and supination — tighter than intact in pronation. 18-hit check: cadaveric studies, technique notes and one

item.title: Research Ideas — 2026-09-08
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Wags Postdoc — Research Ideas, 2026-09-08 (Show Notes) 15 ideas. Top pick: a systematic review of repair tension in rotator cuff repair — 59 primary reports, zero systematic reviews ever. ⚠️ This episode covers two weeks. The scheduled 2026-08-31 run did not fire — no report, no episode — so the literature window here is doubled and that week's slate is permanently lost. This round also ran a day late. Flagged in the report for Swagner Chief. Every gap below was proven with a live PubMed query and hit count, recorded in full in the report. Ideas are starting points, not protocols; the honesty flags stated in the episode are repeated here. --- Clinical — Shoulder Arthroplasty 1. Pectoralis major transfer vs subscapularis repair at the time of reverse shoulder arthroplasty. The only direct comparison in existence (n=27 vs 42, one centre, one implant) found the transfer better on every internal-rotation endpoint, driven by 31% subscapularis retear against zero transfer failures. 16-hit check; the 8-review systematic-review shelf is entirely about repair. ⚠️ Verify the practice does enough transfers at the index operation. 2 / 2 / 3 2. External validation of preoperative hemoglobin strata before shoulder arthroplasty. Sex-specific thresholds derived three weeks ago by a method that is notoriously sample-dependent, with stepwise increases in complications, wound problems and 2-year infection. 16-hit check: no external validation exists. Cheapest idea on the slate — every variable already captured. ⚠️ Infection endpoint will be event-sparse; make transfusion primary. 2 / 3 / 2 Clinical — Rotator Cuff 3. What is the repair tension in a human cuff repair, and does it predict healing? A rat model found a bell-shaped dose–response with a sweet zone at 0.10–0.12 N/mm² — under-tensioning heals nearly as badly as over-tensioning. 47-hit check: the clinical literature uses "low tension" as a categorical label and nobody measures it in a patient. ⚠️ Needs an intraoperative tensiometer that is not standard OR equipment; ordinal surgeon-graded fallback offered. 3 / 1 / 3 4. Randomized trial of tranexamic acid with opioid consumption as the primary endpoint after arthroscopic cuff repair. Three observational reports agree (including a 7,645-per-group matched cohort showing fewer opioid prescriptions at 30 days and 1 year with no increase in pulmonary embolism or infection) and a published JSES letter exchange disputes it. Randomized check → 2 hits, neither an RCT with an opioid primary endpoint; every existing study counts prescriptions, not consumption. ⚠️ The hypothesis is not novel — the randomization and measured-consumption endpoint are. Not an SR opportunity: that shelf holds 16 reviews. 3 / 3 / 2 Clinical — Shoulder Arthroscopy, Scapula, Instability 5. Does fusion grade predict function after scapulothoracic arthrodesis — and does the preoperative stabilization test predict anything? Both halves are now in print one cycle apart: a level-specific CT fusio

item.title: Research Ideas — 2026-08-24
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Research Ideas — 2026-08-24 The companion show to Tutor: each week the Postdoc turns the new literature into concrete, gap-justified study ideas. Thirteen ideas this week — 6 clinical, 3 systematic reviews, 2 database, 2 national incidence — every one with a live PubMed novelty check and its hit count. ⭐ Top pick — who actually receives enabling technology in shoulder arthroplasty. Navigated shoulder replacement grew from 654 to 9,777 cases a year between 2017 and 2023 in one manufacturer's series; the Australian registry has now tested navigation against revision in 5,236 arthroplasties and found no difference; 74% of the American public believes robotics improves implant positioning; and a propensity-matched analysis with 84,767 patients per arm shows socially disadvantaged patients undergo shoulder arthroplasty at 3.14% versus 5.78% — access, not durability. Nobody has asked who is on the receiving end of the technology. 42 records screened on utilization, 33 on disparities: no national utilization study, no equity analysis of any kind. ⭐ Best systematic review — automated measurement of glenoid bone loss. At least sixteen primary studies since 2017 developing or validating automated and AI-based measurement of glenoid bone loss and instability lesions — and a tight systematic-review filter returns zero hits, ever. AI in rotator cuff imaging already has 7 reviews; AI in wrist imaging has 31. The clinical stake is that a few percentage points of measured bone loss moves a patient from Bankart repair, to Bankart with remplissage, to Latarjet — so measurement error converts directly into a different operation. Highest-yield clinical idea — turning the external-rotation lag threshold into a transfer-selection rule. A new cohort derived cut-offs (active external rotation 25° in adduction, 40° in abduction, abduction lag <25°; AUC 0.74–0.76) separating who achieves functional external rotation with reverse arthroplasty alone. Those thresholds identify exactly the patient offered a tendon transfer — and have never been validated, nor used to stratify a reverse-alone versus reverse-plus-transfer comparison. The full slate Clinical 1. Does the new hand-behind-back classification (κ 0.945 vs 0.599 for vertebral level) correspond to a measurable motion strategy? A dynamic-radiography anchor. 2. Reverse arthroplasty for chronic locked anterior dislocation — motion restored, patient-reported function not (36.2 vs 56.6), on n=17. ⚠️ Rare: multicentre or not at all. 3. ⭐ The external-rotation threshold as a transfer-selection rule. 4. Does scapular mechanics actually mediate recovery after cuff repair? A randomised trial just improved the mechanics without moving any patient-reported score. 5. Is the glenoid track you measure the one the patient has? 4D CT put the in vivo track at 74.6% of glenoid width against the ~83% static convention. ⚠️ Needs 4D CT — dynamic radiography cannot do this. 6. "Debride and wait" for chronic dynamic scaphoid instability — 54

item.title: Research Ideas — 2026-08-17
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Wags Postdoc — Research Ideas, 2026-08-17 Companion show to Tutor: where Tutor covers the week's new upper-extremity literature, this episode turns it into gap-justified study ideas. Fifteen ideas this week — 7 clinical, 4 systematic reviews, 2 database, 2 incidence. Every PubMed hit count quoted was run live; every PMID was verified. Ideas are starting points, not protocols. Housekeeping: this round fired on its scheduled Monday slot — the first on-time Monday since 2026-07-20. Episode deliberately tightened after last week's 24-minute overrun; rejected topics get one line each at the end. This week's theme: bone Four of the fifteen ideas come off a single finding. A Michigan study of 831 consecutive total shoulder arthroplasties found that among high-risk patients, only 50% had a preoperative bone density scan and 13% were on any osteoporosis medication — while planning-CT Hounsfield units separated the risk groups cleanly. Clinical ideas 1. Does opportunistic CT bone density add anything to FRAX? Three papers correlate shoulder CT density with the clinical fracture-risk score; two others show CT density predicts complications. A 4-hit search found nobody has tested whether the CT improves prediction over the risk score. Needs no new imaging — the CTs are already in PACS. 3 / 3 / 3 2. Prospective validation of the C. acnes acid-production phenotype. Derived on 40 banked, deliberately selected isolates with an AUC of only 0.72; the authors call it hypothesis-generating. ⚠️ Needs a microbiology laboratory partner. 3 / 2 / 3 3. Middle versus lower trapezius tendon transfer. Two transfers for two different tear patterns; the only direct comparison in print is cadaveric. ⚠️ Depends on whether the practice does enough middle transfers — check the case log. 3 / 2 / 3 4. ⭐ What does pectoralis minor release actually do to the scapula? AJSM is running a published letter-and-response called "The Paradox of Pectoralis Minor Release Versus Repair in Scapular Dyskinesis." One camp releases the muscle for thoracic outlet syndrome; the other now repairs it during Latarjet to prevent dyskinesis. A tight search returned 2 hits — a review and a technique paper. Nobody has ever measured scapular kinematics before and after the release. This group owns the operation, the DDR platform that measures it, and the winging clinic. 3 / 3 / 3 — top pick 5. Scapulothoracic abnormal motion type and generalized hyperlaxity in the surgically treated unstable shoulder. Type 2 motion tracks with Beighton score in athletes but carries no functional penalty there; untested in the hyperlax surgical patient. ⚠️ Must be prospective. 2 / 2 / 2 6. What is the clinical exam worth for foveal TFCC tears? Only 21 of 73 positive ulnar fovea signs had a foveal tear; arthroscopic agreement collapses to κ 0.32 outside central tears. item.title: Research Ideas — 2026-08-13
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Wags Postdoc — Research Ideas — 2026-08-13 (Show Notes) Companion to Tutor. Each week the Postdoc turns the new upper-extremity literature into concrete, gap-checked study ideas. These are starting points, not protocols. Full write-up with every PubMed query + hit count: 50 System/Agents/Wags Postdoc Reports/2026-08-13 Research Ideas.md. This week: 15 ideas — Clinical 8, Systematic Review 3, Database 2, Incidence 2. Ran three days late (the Monday slot did not fire). The wrist-arthroscopy feed returned zero new in-window articles, so Tutor deliberately widened to twelve months and delivered a one-time catch-up of 27 never-digested papers — the richest single input this program has had, and the source of two of this week's strongest ideas. Top pick — Medial scapular winging in neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome (Clinical): the field is arguing about this in print right now — a March study associating long thoracic nerve variants with medial winging in TOS drew a formal letter and author response in the August issue of the same journal. Both sides are arguing on anatomical and cross-sectional grounds; neither has outcome data. An 8-hit check found nobody has reported winging prevalence in a surgical nTOS cohort, and nobody has reported outcomes stratified by it. Eric holds the assets on both sides: the arthroscopic pectoralis minor release series, the nTOS diagnostic-criteria consensus he led, the scapular dyskinesia differentiation framework, and both clinics. Cheapest high-yield idea — Gripping-view ulnar variance before arthroscopic TFCC debridement (Clinical): one 30-patient series split patients purely on whether ulnar variance reaches 1 mm on a gripping PA view — 7 revisions versus 0, 7 of 17 versus 1 of 13 failing to return to work. A 7-hit check found the index paper is the only one on point. One extra radiograph. Strongest systematic review — Dorsal (non-Palmer) TFCC tears: 14 indexed reports, ~6 clinical series, 0 systematic reviews ever. Three papers in twelve months all assert the lesion is common and commonly missed at arthroscopy — and none reports a denominator. The structural twin of last week's volar scapholunate top pick. Ideas Clinical 1. A validated instability risk score for reverse shoulder arthroplasty (new SR lists 11 risk factors and calls them hypothesis-generating; 2-hit check, no model exists). ⚠️ low event rate — likely multicenter. 2. Standardized stepwise reduction in proximal humerus fracture plating — does the 12-fold radiographic advantage reach the patient? (index study measured radiographs only). 3. External validation of the 19 mm² biceps sheath effusion MRI threshold against arthroscopy (threshold was derived against expert visual judgment — circular until somebody scopes). 4. Systemic perioperative methylprednisolone in arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (RCT). All 5 methylprednisolone-plus-cuff hits are local/periarticular injection. item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Wags Postdoc — Research Ideas — 2026-08-03 (Show Notes) Companion to Tutor. Each week the Postdoc turns the new upper-extremity literature into concrete, gap-checked study ideas. These are starting points, not protocols. Full write-up with every PubMed query + hit count: 50 System/Agents/Wags Postdoc Reports/2026-08-03 Research Ideas.md. This week: 13 ideas — Clinical 6, Systematic Review 3, Database 2, Incidence 2. Two weeks of literature in one round (no slate ran 2026-07-27), and the wrist-arthroscopy feed broke a six-week dry spell with three J Wrist Surg papers — one of which produced the top pick. Top pick — The volar component of scapholunate ligament injury (Systematic Review): ~25 primary reports, zero systematic reviews ever. The adjacent syntheses cover dorsal capsulodesis (2025) and partial SL injuries (2024); neither touches the volar side. Arthroscopy is the test that identifies the volar tear, which puts the diagnostic step inside the wrist-arthroscopy program. No data-feasibility risk — it's a synthesis. Runner-up — Dual- vs. single-plate fixation of proximal humerus fractures (Systematic Review + meta-analysis): 53 primary reports, 0 systematic reviews/meta-analyses; the 8 existing reviews are all narrative. This week's 141-patient cohort found 22.7% vs. 5.4% reoperation favouring dual plating — a large effect from one non-randomized centre, which is what meta-analysis is for. Ideas Clinical 1. Does scapular-predominant motion on dynamic digital radiography precede acromial/scapular-spine stress fracture after reverse arthroplasty? (Eric's own SHR paper + this month's SPECT/CT stress paper — two halves of one hypothesis; 1-hit, unrelated, novelty check.) 2. Diagnostic yield and management impact of arthroscopy in the equivocal painful shoulder replacement (only modern series is n=29). 3. Bioinductive collagen implant in high-risk / transfer-candidate cuff repairs — the population this week's 112-patient study skipped (its benefit concentrated in small-medium, low-Goutallier tears). 4. Preoperative suprascapular neuropathy as a predictor of failure after tendon transfer (rat model shows entrapment blocks healing; existing meta-analyses tested release-as-treatment, not neuropathy-as-predictor). 5. Remplissage fixation position vs. external-rotation loss — clinical test of this week's in-silico dose-response (9 hits, all biomechanical). 6. Prevalence and treatment of the volar scapholunate component in a consecutive arthroscopic series (clinical companion to the top pick). Systematic Reviews 7. Volar scapholunate component — diagnosis and volar-based repair outcomes (TOP PICK) — 25 primary, 0 SR ever. 8. Dual- vs. single-plate proximal humerus fixation — 53 primary, 0 SR/MA. 9. Diagnostic arthroscopy for the painful shoulder arthroplasty — yield and management impact (partial gap: existing SRs are infection-only and lysis-only). item.title: Research Ideas — 2026-07-20
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Wags Postdoc — Research Ideas — 2026-07-20 (Show Notes) Companion to Tutor. Each week the Postdoc turns the new upper-extremity literature into concrete, gap-checked study ideas. These are starting points, not protocols. Full write-up with every PubMed query + hit count: 50 System/Agents/Wags Postdoc Reports/2026-07-20 Research Ideas.md. This week: 13 ideas — Clinical 7, Systematic Review 2, Database 2, Incidence 2. An imaging-heavy week: both systematic-review ideas are orphans surfaced by this week's radar refresh of the DDR/AI Imaging and Health Disparities programs (which completes the first full pass across all 8 programs). Top pick — Diagnostic accuracy of 4D CT for scapholunate/carpal instability (Systematic Review): 84 primary studies, zero systematic reviews — while MRI, MR-arthrography, and CBCT-arthrography each already have a diagnostic-accuracy review, 4D CT (the modality being promoted as the "new standard") has none. Low data risk, bridges DDR/AI Imaging + Wrist Arthroscopy. Ideas Clinical 1. Validate radiographic LSA/DSA vs CT ground truth in a US RSA registry (from Werthel 2026 CT-offset study). 2. Inlay vs onlay glenoid — clinical loosening/survivorship test of this week's finite-element prediction (multi-institutional; inlay-volume caveat). 3. Does preop GLP-1 use associate with less fatty infiltration/better healing after cuff repair? — human translation of the rat finding (muscle-quality endpoint, not the crowded retear endpoint). 4. Remnant preservation + nanofracture bone-marrow stimulation in high-risk cuff repairs (replicate/extend Milano 2026). 5. MCID/PASS thresholds for arthroscopic pectoralis minor release (the largest series, MGH n=273, reported none). 6. Value of concomitant brachial plexus neurolysis with pec minor release (60% got it, outcomes pooled). 7. Diagnostic concordance of DDR/4D-CT vs arthroscopic Geissler grade for scapholunate instability (clinical companion to the top pick). Systematic Reviews 8. DDR for upper-extremity kinematics — validity & reliability (36 primary, 0 SR). 9. 4D CT diagnostic accuracy for scapholunate/carpal instability (TOP PICK) (84 primary, 0 SR). Database 10. Disparities in access to perioperative GLP-1 agonists before upper-extremity surgery (studied in TKA/THA only; fuses GLP-1 + FOSSIL). 11. Weight-stratified antibiotic prophylaxis and PJI after shoulder arthroplasty (from this week's synovial-fluid PK study). Incidence 12. National trends in scapholunate ligament surgery, repair vs reconstruction vs salvage (2012–2024). 13. National incidence/trends of shoulder PJI and two-stage revision (2010–2024). Honesty flags (carried into the audio) - Wrist-arthroscopy Tutor track empty for a 4th straight week — the wrist idea leans on DDR/4D-CT literature. - No PubMed MCP this session; all counts from live NCBI E-utilities. - Ideas A1, A2, C2 carry explicit data-feasibility caveats (post-op CT availability; inlay volume; claims dose granularity). - No figure this week — search sets n

item.title: Research Ideas — 2026-07-14
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Wags Postdoc — Research Ideas — 2026-07-14 Fourteen upper-extremity research ideas from this week's Wags Postdoc slate. For each: a brief summary of the current literature, why it is novel, and how it would contribute. Companion to the Tutor literature podcast; same two hosts. Top pick: Systematic review — comparative treatment outcomes for volar wrist ganglia (arthroscopic vs. open vs. aspiration). Clinical — Shoulder Arthroplasty: (1) Multi-institutional replication of the stem-lateralization/tuberosity-healing dose-response relationship in fracture reverse shoulder arthroplasty. (2) Multi-institutional replication of a cephalosporin-allergy/prophylaxis revision-risk finding. Clinical — Rotator Cuff: (3) Expanded cohort of biceps autograft "smash" patch augmentation in high-risk repairs. (4) Telerehabilitation non-inferiority specific to tendon transfer (LTT/LDT) patients. Clinical — Shoulder Arthroscopy / Instability: (5) US non-military external validation of posterior labral repair MCID/PASS thresholds. (6) Retention/loss-to-follow-up protocol for the minimally invasive TOS and instability clinic. Clinical — Wrist Arthroscopy: (7) Empirical (non-modeled) cost/recurrence comparison for volar wrist ganglion treatment pathways. (8) Portal-specific nerve injury/complication audit in wrist arthroscopy. Systematic Reviews: (9) Comparative treatment outcomes for volar wrist ganglia — arthroscopic vs. open vs. aspiration (top pick). (10) Catheter irrigation vs. open washout for surgically treated pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis. Database: (11) PearlDiver — early national adoption and 90-day complications of dual-mobility CMC implant arthroplasty. (12) NSQIP — 30-day VTE/wound complications after tendon transfer (LTT/LDT) vs. arthroscopic rotator cuff repair. Incidence/Epidemiology: (13) National incidence/treatment-selection trends for displaced proximal humerus fractures in the elderly (nonoperative vs. hemiarthroplasty vs. reverse shoulder arthroplasty), 2015-2024. (14) National incidence/adoption trajectory of dual-mobility CMC implant arthroplasty since US approval. Honesty note: a dozen systematic-review candidates were tested and disqualified this week because genuine recent reviews already exist (cubital tunnel technique, lateral epicondylitis, scapular winging reconstruction, robotic scaphoid fixation, ALPSA repair, tuberosity healing/GT repair after RSA, SLAC wrist, pyrocarbon arthroplasty, wrist denervation, telerehabilitation, acromial fracture after RSA, midcarpal instability) — the full scan log with every query and hit count is in the Research Ideas write-up. The two systematic reviews that did qualify are framed precisely: B1 (volar wrist ganglion) has a real 12-year-old gap; B2 (flexor tenosynovitis technique) is a narrower reframing of a topic whose broader question was already reviewed in 2024. No roster forwards ("Wags Research Assistant" emails) this week.

item.title: Research Ideas — 2026-07-06
item.itunes:author: Eric R. Wagner, MD, MSc
item.description: Wags Postdoc — Research Ideas — 2026-07-06 Sixteen upper-extremity research ideas from this week's Wags Postdoc slate. For each: a brief summary of the current literature, why it is novel, and how it would contribute. Companion to the Tutor literature podcast; same two hosts. Top pick: External validation of the postoperative-day-7 D-dimer cutoff for silent DVT after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair, extended to tendon-transfer patients. Clinical — Shoulder Arthroplasty: (1) Validating the new HUMBL humeral bone-loss classification at a second US center. (2) Perioperative GLP-1 agonist use and complications after total/reverse shoulder replacement. Clinical — Rotator Cuff: (3) Lower trapezius transfer vs. superior capsular reconstruction, using newly defined MCID/PASS thresholds. (4) Validating the POD-7 D-dimer DVT-screening cutoff after arthroscopic cuff repair (top pick). Clinical — Shoulder Arthroscopy / nTOS: (5) Arthroscopic pectoralis minor release vs. endoscopic brachial plexus release for neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome. (6) Remplissage failure thresholds stratified by glenoid bone-loss severity. Clinical — Wrist Arthroscopy: (7) Arthroscopic scaphoid nonunion fixation — union by location and cartilage-cap biology (novelty check needs re-run). (8) Thumb CMC arthritis in young patients — arthroscopy vs. fusion vs. LRTI (novelty check needs re-run). Systematic Reviews: (9) Remplissage outcomes stratified by bone-loss severity. (10) TFCC repair technique comparison (all-inside vs. outside-in vs. foveal reattachment). Database: (11) PearlDiver GLP-1 agonists and 90-day complications after shoulder arthroplasty. (12) NSQIP wrist/elbow arthroscopy complications not captured in standard fields (nerve/soft-tissue injury), with a local chart-review supplement. Incidence/Epidemiology: (13) National incidence and trends in elbow arthroscopy, 2010–2024 (novelty unconfirmed). (14) National incidence of neurogenic TOS surgery (novelty needs cleaner search). Honesty note: four ideas (both wrist clinical ideas and both incidence studies) rest on novelty searches that returned thin results on narrow queries and need a cleaner re-run before committing resources. Full write-up with evidence tables and every query is in the Research Ideas Word document.
